lessons.text: Top lesson: One win doesn't prove my Chovy-over-Rookie call, because the debate showed GEN took early tempo and the map, not that Chovy won lane. Next time I'll back the side whose players are stronger across several roles, especially jungle and bot, since that's what builds early tempo, and not lean on a single marquee lane. (from Swiss GEN vs IG; picked GEN, actual GEN 1-0)

Jungle lesson: The early game still decides everything, so when a big region gap is flagged, I should confirm it shows up as first-15-minute tempo (jungle pathing, lane priority, first objectives) and not lean on star names or records. I can also borrow Mid's draft point: a deep draft is what hands you that early priority, so I'll check whether a team's picks set up the first tower and dragon before I raise my confidence. (from Swiss GEN vs IG; picked GEN, actual GEN 1-0)

Mid lesson: Fearless depth still decides series, but I should show it through specific draft outcomes, like which jungle and lane picks give GEN early tempo and priority, rather than a general "more answers" claim. I also shouldn't lean on a league-gap argument or domestic records unless the scouting report flags a BIG REGION GAP, because the draft and the star's pool are the real case. (from Swiss GEN vs IG; picked GEN, actual GEN 1-0)

ADC lesson: The 37-10 vs 18-25 series gap set a sound 79%, but my reasoning also leaned on a Chovy-vs-Rookie story I never backed with lane numbers. Next time I'll price the confidence only from measurable inputs (series records, head-to-heads, game length tendencies) and check Jungle's point that early tempo decided it by looking at first-objective and gold-at-15 stats before crediting any one matchup. (from Swiss GEN vs IG; picked GEN, actual GEN 1-0)

Support lesson: Team chemistry decides games, but I should anchor that read in things I can see, like comebacks, composure after setbacks, and clean early-game coordination (GEN's tempo is where "locked-in" actually showed up), rather than claiming the vibes were obvious afterward. I should also bring in region only when the scouting report flags a big gap, and otherwise let the team's mood and cohesion carry the pick. (from Swiss GEN vs IG; picked GEN, actual GEN 1-0)
